title: Europe cancels planned upgrades for Ariane 6 rocket
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) has canceled the 'Block 3' upgrades for the Ariane 6 rocket, including the lightweight ICARUS upper stage, due to high costs and financial concerns. While the Ariane 6 has successfully launched eight missions, its future is uncertain as European ministers hesitate to fund further upgrades or increased production. The rocket currently relies on significant subsidies (32-38 million euros per launch) and faces challenges competing with reusable rockets from the U.S. and China. ESA is considering scaling up production but must weigh the financial viability of subsidizing commercial launches against investing in next-generation reusable rockets.
key_points: The Ariane 6 rocket has successfully completed eight missions since its debut, providing Europe with reliable access to orbit.
The 'Block 3' upgrades, including the lightweight ICARUS upper stage, have been canceled due to cost concerns, impacting future science missions like a probe to Saturn’s moon Enceladus.

Europe invested approximately 3.6 billion euros in Ariane 6’s development, with ongoing subsidies of 32-38 million euros per launch, totaling over 100 million euros per launch before customer payments.
Arianespace has not disclosed the exact cost per launch, but estimates suggest it ranges between 80-100 million euros.
Amazon is a major commercial customer, with 18 contracted launches for its Project Kuiper constellation, though Europe may be losing money on these missions.
ESA aims to increase Ariane 6’s launch cadence from 9-10 to potentially 12-20 launches per year but requires additional investment in production and logistics.
European ministers must decide whether to scale up Ariane 6 production or invest in next-generation reusable rockets to compete with U.S. and Chinese advancements.
The decision on scaling production, expected by the end of the year, will reveal Europe’s long-term strategy for Ariane 6 and its space launch capabilities.
